main_text.p: In qualitate, cum materia fovendo igni inepta est, ut ligna viridia.
In quantitate, cum ignis nimia materiae copia obruitur.
Ex parte ipsius ignis, fit μαρανσις[?] violenta, cum vel excedit, vel deficit.
Excedit mediocritatem, & praeter modum augetur, aut ex sese, propter frigidi aëris defectum: aut accessione majoris flammae.
Deficit à mediocritate & minuitur aut sua sponte paulatim expirans: aut per vim à materia avellitur.
Avellitur autem vel motu & agitatione nimia: vel majoris flammae appro-pinquitate[?].
Ignis si ab alio corrumpitur, dicitur σβέσις[?] extinctio, quę fit à frigore contrario.Σβέσης[?].
Hoc modo extinguitur vel saltem imminuitur Ignis, aut à nimio gelu: aut ab humore balnei, & aëris nebulosi: aut ab aquae effusione.
Sed satis de Igni, cujus effectus in re-rum natura sunt mirabiles, unde in ge-nere nata est Pyrotechnia, & in specie variae artes Feuerfunst.

page.notes: The Greek word after "fit" (read as μαρανσις) is doubtful; the Greek in the text and in the margin is also doubtful and may be printed with a different spelling. The margin note "Σβέσης." is read as printed. The "pinquitate" line is doubtful. "Feuerfunst" is set in black letter. The page has faint show-through from the reverse side, which is not transcribed.
